marta: Ran the new adaptive per-route governor today. 95th looks better on interactive chat routes but worse on embedding-heavy calls. digging in :eyes:
kai: numbers?
marta: quick snapshot:
```
chat-route: p95 -12% (was 120ms -> 106ms)
embed-route: p95 +18% (was 85ms -> 100ms)
overall tail count increased on embed-route by ~22%
KV cache hit-rate dropped from 81% -> 63% for embed-route during peak
```
alex: interesting. could this be kernel selection flip/flop? if microbatch sizes shrink we might be hitting different GEMM paths and recompile penalties.
marta: yep, profile shows more kernel switches when token budget throttles batches under 8 examples. recompile + extra memcpy ~= 6-9ms on those calls.
ryan: what about queue policy? are we forcing strict token caps that fragment batches? maybe try a soft cap or an emergency fill threshold.
marta: current policy is `hard-token-budget` per tier (config snippet):
```
governor: adaptive
tiers:
  gold:
    token_budget_target: 200
  standard:
    token_budget_target: 120
  embed-heavy:
    token_budget_target: 60
queue_policy: hard-first-fit
microbatch_min: 1
microbatch_max: 4
```
kai: that embed-heavy tier budget (60) seems low for typical embed requests — they come with long contexts and trigger KV misses. KV miss penalties amplify when batches are tiny.
ryan: try `soft-preempt` where we reserve N tokens iff KV hit-rate < 70%. that gives prioritized KV-friendly aggregation. also bump microbatch_min to 2 to avoid tiny GEMM paths.
marta: will run A/B: (A) soft-preempt + reserve 10 tokens + microbatch_min=2, (B) keep hard budget but increase embed tier to 100.
alex: also instrument kernel selection tags in the trace so we can correlate p95 to kernel id and memcpy counts. add counter `kernel_switches` and `gpu_memcpy_us`.
infra-bot: perf-canary: deploy/ops/1974200199 started -> canary-id=ci-1974-adapt1 :rocket:
marta: thanks, infra-bot. kicking off 6 canary runs now. will post TL;DR when done. :thumbsup: 
kai: if A reduces kernel switches and KV misses without increasing cost too much, prefer it. otherwise lean to B and revisit cache TTL/eviction thresholds.
ryan: might also be worth a short experiment with kernel-pin: prefer large-matmul path for embed route when seq_len>1024 to avoid runtime path flip. cheap to test.
marta: adding kernel-pin flag to experiment matrix. starting runs now, ETA ~45m.
alex: ping when results in — also include sample traces for a few regressed requests so we can repro locally. :thinking:
marta: will attach traces in the follow-up thread.
